title: Tech Note: Scanning Text and BLOBs Efficiently or Testing Performance Meaningfully
author: David Adams

historical_commentary.text: This note investigates a very specific, dramatic 4th Dimension 2004 performance pitfall (scanning text through a pointer being roughly 700x slower than scanning it directly) and uses it as a case study for how to design and interpret meaningful performance tests, concluding with practical pass-by-value/pass-by-pointer rules of thumb. The specific benchmark numbers are tied to the 4D 2004.2 compiler/runtime of the era and are now obsolete given two decades of runtime, compiler, and memory-management improvements, but the methodological lesson — that raw ratios can be misleading without considering absolute time and real-world impact — remains a genuinely useful, still-relevant piece of engineering advice for any performance testing today.
related_updates: 4D's compiler and runtime performance characteristics for text/BLOB operations have changed substantially since 2004/2005; these exact benchmark ratios no longer apply to current versions
The general performance-testing methodology and pass-by-value/pointer trade-off reasoning remain applicable programming principles
